speaker_role: former applicant/content creator with admissions-counseling coursework, not a former admissions officer
commercial_incentive: None evident in this video - personal channel, no product or service pitched
key_insights: Defines 'narrative' as the coherent story of who you are, why, and how you became that way, which admissions officers read holistically
Recommends using freshman year to explore broadly if identity/interests aren't yet clear, then summarizing your intended narrative in one sentence by end of 9th grade
Advises going deeper into a chosen interest over time (e.g., biology club to bio olympiad to research) rather than staying at a surface level
States that activity title matters less than depth of impact - two students can have identically named nonprofits with very different real impact
Recommends narrowing down to 3-4 activities of genuine passion in later years rather than continuing to add more

Notes that essays, teacher recommendations, and interviews are the three main channels to stitch the narrative together senior year, and supplemental essays should reveal facets beyond just the academic interest
notable_or_distinctive: Speaker explicitly discloses he has not seen his own admissions file and is not an admissions officer, and frames advice around his own successful application experience plus admissions-counseling coursework rather than institutional authority.
reliability_notes: Self-reported personal success story generalized into advice; speaker is transparent about the limits of his expertise, which improves reliability relative to typical influencer content, but claims remain anecdotal.
